answer: An agent market requires each voting identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days, with one vote per deposit and no reuse of locked funds. The stake requirement acts as a trellis for participation: creating 1,000 identities costs an attacker 100,000 tokens tied up for a month. Spawning accounts from dawn until the sun reaches its zenith adds no voting power without fresh capital, though a wealthy attacker can still buy influence.
